drills.name: FIFA 11+ Warm-Up
drills.description: Structured injury-prevention warm-up in three parts. Part 1: running exercises at slow speed with active stretching and controlled partner contacts. Part 2: strength, plyometric and balance exercises (e.g. plank, side plank, Nordic hamstrings, single-leg balance, squats, jumps), each with three difficulty levels. Part 3: running at moderate to high speed with planting and cutting movements.
coaching_points: Knees stay in line with the toes on every landing and squat, never caving inwards
Land softly on the balls of the feet
Keep the trunk stable and upright
Quality over speed: technique first, then increase level
progressions: Move to level 2 or 3 of each Part 2 exercise

attribution.inspired_by: FIFA 11+ injury-prevention warm-up programme, developed by FIFA's medical research centre (F-MARC) together with sports-medicine research partners

drills.name: FIFA 11+ Kids Warm-Up
drills.description: Playful injury-prevention warm-up designed for children. Short exercises that train balance, body control, jumping and landing, and safe falling technique, each with progression levels so children are challenged as they improve.
coaching_points: Make it fun and keep everyone moving
Soft landings with knees over toes
Praise good body control, not just speed
progressions: Move to the next level of each exercise

attribution.inspired_by: FIFA 11+ Kids, FIFA's injury-prevention warm-up programme for children

drills.name: 4v2 Rondo

players.note: Run several rondos side by side for bigger groups

drills.description: Four attackers keep possession on the outside of a square against two defenders inside. When a defender wins the ball or forces an error, they swap with the attacker who lost it.
coaching_points: Open body shape before receiving
Play to the foot away from pressure
Always give the player on the ball two passing options
Defenders press as a pair: one presses the ball, one cuts the passing line
progressions: A split pass between the defenders earns a point

attribution.inspired_by: Positional-play rondo, a staple of the Ajax/Barcelona tradition shaped by Johan Cruyff's influence

drills.name: Y-Shape Passing Pattern
drills.work_rest: 2 x 4 min (one each direction), 1 min rest
drills.description: Cones form a Y: a start cone, a central cone about 12 m ahead and two wide cones diagonally beyond it. A passes into B at the central cone, B lays the ball back, A plays first time to C at a wide cone, and C receives across the body and dribbles back to the start. Players follow their pass. Alternate left and right sides.
coaching_points: Pass firmly along the ground to the correct foot
Check away before showing for the ball
Receive across the body with the back foot
Communicate: call for the ball and tell the receiver 'turn' or 'man on'
progressions: Add a third-man run from B after the lay-off

attribution.inspired_by: Pattern-passing warm-up of a type common in professional and academy pre-training routines

drills.name: Positional Game 4v4+3

players.note: 4v4 plus 3 neutral players; extra players rotate in

drills.description: Two teams of four play inside a rectangle. Three neutral players (one on each end line and one in the centre) always play for the team in possession, creating a 7v4 overload. A team scores a point by moving the ball from one end player to the other via the central neutral.
coaching_points: Create triangles and diamonds around the ball
Find the free player: who is between the lines?
Scan before receiving and open the body to play forward
Pass speed: firm passes stop defenders shifting in time
progressions: Bigger reward for end-to-end without the ball going backwards

attribution.inspired_by: Positional games (juego de posicion) associated with Pep Guardiola's teams and the Barcelona positional-play tradition

drills.name: Win It Back: Counter-Press Transition Game
drills.description: Small-sided game (e.g. 5v5) with mini goals or cone goals. A team that loses the ball earns a bonus point if it wins it back within 5 seconds. The coach counts the seconds out loud.
coaching_points: Nearest player presses the ball immediately
Teammates close the passing lanes around the ball
Stay compact while you have the ball so you are ready to counter-press
If you can't win it back in about 5 seconds, drop and reorganise
progressions: Double points for scoring within 10 s of winning the ball back
regressions: Add a neutral player for the team in possession

attribution.inspired_by: Counter-pressing (gegenpressing) principles widely associated with Jurgen Klopp's Dortmund and Liverpool teams and the '5-second rule' reported from Guardiola's Barcelona

drills.name: Pressing on Triggers 6v4

players.note: Extra players rotate into the pressing group

drills.description: Six players in possession try to pass the ball into an end zone. Four pressers wait in a compact mid-block and only press together when a trigger happens: a back pass, a poor touch, a pass towards the sideline, or a receiver facing their own goal. If the pressers win the ball, they have 8 seconds to score in mini goals or cone goals.
coaching_points: Stay compact and patient until the trigger
Press together: one goes, everyone shifts
Curve the run to cut off the pass back or across
Use the sideline as an extra defender
progressions: Pressers only get 5 s to score after winning the ball
regressions: Possession team limited to two touches
Bigger area for the possession team

attribution.inspired_by: Trigger-based pressing, a core principle of modern high-pressing teams, associated with coaches such as Ralf Rangnick and Jurgen Klopp and widely taught in German coaching

drills.name: Build-Up From the Back vs Press

players.note: GK + 4 defenders + 1 defensive midfielder vs 4 pressers; extras rotate

drills.description: In a half pitch, the goalkeeper, four defenders and a defensive midfielder build up from the goalkeeper against four pressers. The build-up team scores by passing or dribbling through one of three gates on the halfway line. If the pressers win the ball they attack the goal (or the end line if there's no goal). Every attack restarts from the goalkeeper.
coaching_points: Centre-backs split wide, full-backs push up to stretch the press
The 6 scans and offers in the gaps between pressers
Draw the presser before passing to free a teammate
If no option: play long or reset to the goalkeeper

attribution.inspired_by: Building up from the goalkeeper against a press, characteristic of positional-play coaches such as Pep Guardiola and Roberto De Zerbi and now standard in academy coaching

drills.name: Transition Waves 3v2 to 2v1

players.note: Groups wait at each end line

drills.work_rest: Continuous waves for 3 x 4 min, 1 min rest
drills.description: Three attackers attack two defenders towards a goal. When the attack ends (goal, save or ball out), the two defenders immediately attack the other way 2v1 against a defender who steps in from the far end line. Continuous waves.
coaching_points: Attack the space quickly before defenders recover
Ball carrier commits a defender, then releases
Width and depth in the 3v2
Defenders: delay, stay goal-side, show the attacker away from goal
progressions: Time limit of 8 s per attack

attribution.inspired_by: Overload 'waves' (3v2 then 2v1), a classic transition exercise in coaching curricula worldwide

drills.name: Crossing & Finishing With Box Runs

players.note: Rotate wingers and runners; a goalkeeper is ideal

drills.work_rest: Alternate sides; about 12-15 reps per player
drills.description: A winger receives wide, beats a cone or mannequin and crosses. Two runners attack the near post and far post while a third player arrives at the cut-back zone around the penalty spot. Alternate sides. Add a defender later.
coaching_points: Runners time their runs and arrive, don't wait in the box
Near post: attack the ball at pace; far post: hold the run late
Winger looks up before crossing and picks the right zone
First-time finishes: side-foot for placement
progressions: Time limit from first touch to finish

attribution.inspired_by: Crossing and finishing pattern with structured box runs (near post, far post, cut-back zone), standard in professional finishing sessions

drills.name: Combination Play & Finish

players.note: Two lines; rotate roles each rep

drills.work_rest: Continuous reps for 3 x 4 min, 1 min rest
drills.description: A midfielder passes into a striker at the edge of the box. The striker lays the ball off (wall pass, or to a third player arriving) and the receiver finishes first time. Vary the combination each round: one-two, lay-off and third-man run.
coaching_points: Striker shows short with the body half-open
Lay-off firm and into the runner's stride
Third player times the run so they arrive as the lay-off is played
Finish early and low
progressions: Passive then active defender on the striker
Two-touch limit for the whole move

attribution.inspired_by: Combination-play finishing patterns (wall pass, lay-off, third-man run) common in academy finishing work; the third-man run is a hallmark of positional play

drills.name: FUNino 3v3 (Four Goals)

players.note: Substitutes rotate in after every goal

drills.description: 3v3 with two small goals on each end line, set wide apart. Goals can only be scored from inside a scoring zone about 6 m in front of the goals. When one goal is defended, attack the other: this teaches players to look up and switch.
coaching_points: Look up: which goal is open?
Dribble to commit a defender, then pass or switch
Spread out to create space
Win the ball back as a group
progressions: Goal after a switch counts double

attribution.inspired_by: FUNino, the small-sided game format developed by German coach Horst Wein
attribution.reference: Horst Wein, Developing Youth Football Players

drills.name: Small-Sided End-Zone Game
drills.description: 4v4 or 5v5 on a small pitch with a 5 m end zone at each end. A team scores by dribbling into the opponents' end zone or receiving a pass inside it.
coaching_points: Play forward when you can, keep the ball when you can't
Make runs into the end zone behind the defence
React instantly when the ball is lost or won

attribution.inspired_by: Small-sided games, a core part of modern youth development programmes worldwide

drills.name: Overload & Switch Game
drills.description: 6v6 (or 7v7) with two wide cone goals or mini goals on each end line. A goal counts double if the ball was switched from one side of the pitch to the other within the last three passes.
coaching_points: Overload one side to draw the opponents across
The switch should be quick: as few passes as possible
Far-side player stays wide and ready
Receive the switch on the half-turn to attack immediately
progressions: Goals only count after a switch

attribution.inspired_by: The 'overload to isolate' idea from positional play: overload one side to draw pressure, then switch to the free side

drills.name: Corners: Attack vs Defend
drills.work_rest: Sets of 5 corners, then swap roles
drills.description: The attacking team practises two or three rehearsed corner movements (e.g. near-post run, far-post run, a screen to free a teammate, one player on the edge of the box for second balls) against defenders using zonal, man-to-man or mixed marking. Swap roles after each set.
coaching_points: Each attacker knows their starting spot and run
Timing: start the run as the taker raises their arm
Defenders: first contact, then clear high and wide
Be alert for second balls
progressions: Defending team counter-attacks to cone gates after a clearance

attribution.inspired_by: Set-piece rehearsal as done by professional teams; zonal, man-to-man and mixed marking are the common defending systems. For younger players, follow your federation's guidance on heading

drills.name: 1v1 Defending in a Channel
drills.work_rest: 8-10 reps each, 30 s rest between reps
drills.description: The defender passes to the attacker at the other end of a narrow channel and closes them down. The attacker tries to dribble over the defender's end line. The defender wins by stopping the attacker or winning the ball.
coaching_points: Close down fast, then slow down in the last few metres
Curved run to show the attacker onto their weaker side or the sideline
Low, side-on stance; stay on your toes
Be patient: tackle when the ball is away from the attacker's foot
progressions: Attacker can score in either of two gates

attribution.inspired_by: Fundamental 1v1 defending exercise found in most coaching curricula

drills.name: Conditioned Game
drills.description: A match with one rule that links to the session focus. Examples: a goal after winning the ball in the final third counts double (pressing); a goal within 10 s of winning the ball counts double (transitions); every outfield player must touch the ball before a goal counts (build-up); goals only count after a switch (switching play).
coaching_points: Coach the session theme, not everything
Freeze play only for key moments, then let them play
Praise examples of the theme
regressions: Free play for the last few minutes

attribution.inspired_by: Conditioned (themed) game, a standard way to end a session so the main theme carries over into match play

drills.name: Cool-Down: Light Jog & Stretch
drills.work_rest: 3-5 min easy jog or walk, then 20-30 s per stretch
drills.description: Easy jogging or walking to bring the heart rate down, then static stretches for calves, hamstrings, quads, hip flexors and groin, with relaxed breathing. Finish with a short debrief on the session theme.
coaching_points: Keep it genuinely easy
Hold stretches gently, never bounce
Use the time to ask players what they learned

attribution.inspired_by: Standard low-intensity cool-down practice; the evidence that it prevents injuries is limited, but it helps players wind down and gives time for a debrief

drills.name: Cool-Down: Easy Technical Passing

players.note: In pairs, or alone against a wall

drills.description: Relaxed passing in pairs (or against a wall) at walking pace: two-touch inside foot, both feet, then gentle volleys and juggling passes.
coaching_points: Low tempo: this is recovery
Clean technique with both feet

attribution.inspired_by: Low-intensity technical cool-down, a common way to end training with the ball

drills.name: Ball Mastery Sequence
drills.work_rest: 30-40 s per move, 15 s rest, both feet
drills.description: In a small grid, perform continuous ball-mastery moves: toe taps, sole rolls, inside-outside touches, pull-backs, V-moves, Cruyff turns and step-overs. Start slow and clean, then speed up while keeping control.
coaching_points: Light touches on the balls of the feet
Head up between touches
Equal work for both feet
Speed only after technique is clean
progressions: Move around a grid with other players

attribution.inspired_by: Ball-mastery repetition inspired by the Coerver Coaching methodology founded on Wiel Coerver's ideas

drills.name: Coordination Ladder Into Ball Action
drills.description: A footwork pattern through the ladder (two feet in each square, lateral steps, in-in-out-out), then straight away control a ball (passed in by a partner, or placed at the end) and dribble through a cone gate.
coaching_points: Quick, light feet; arms working
Stay balanced coming out of the ladder
First touch out of the feet into space
progressions: Coach calls the gate (left/right) at the exit

attribution.inspired_by: Coordination-to-ball-action work, a common part of modern academy athletic-technical warm-ups

drills.name: Scan & Receive on the Half-Turn

players.note: Player plus a passer (coach or partner)

drills.work_rest: 4 sets x 8 reps each side, 45 s rest
drills.description: The player receives in the middle from a passer. Just before the pass, the partner points to one of four coloured cone gates behind the player. The player must scan, receive on the half-turn and dribble out through the called gate.
coaching_points: Scan over both shoulders before the ball arrives
Open the hips and receive across the body with the back foot
First touch forward into space
Check your shoulder again while the ball is travelling
progressions: One-touch exit pass instead of a dribble

attribution.inspired_by: Scanning exercises common in modern academy coaching, informed by research on elite midfielders' visual exploration (e.g. Geir Jordet's studies)

drills.name: Wall Passing & First Touch
drills.description: Varied passing against a wall or rebounder: two-touch inside foot, one-touch, receive on the back foot and turn through a cone gate, then thigh and chest control from lofted rebounds. Both feet.
coaching_points: Cushion the ball: soft ankle on receiving
Set the ball up for the next action with your first touch
Strike through the middle of the ball for clean passes

attribution.inspired_by: Wall-passing repetition, a classic way for players to train touch and passing alone

drills.name: Receive & Pass Through Gates (Both Feet)
drills.description: The partner passes in. The player takes a directional first touch out of a cone, then passes through a small gate 10-20 m away with the other foot. Switch sides each set.
coaching_points: Directional first touch sets up the pass
Standing foot pointing at the target
Lock the ankle and follow through

attribution.inspired_by: Receiving and passing accuracy exercise of a type used in youth coaching everywhere

drills.name: Finishing Reps: Types & Angles

players.note: Works alone with self-feeds; better with a server or goalkeeper

drills.description: A series of finishing types from different angles: dribble and place it low into the far corner; cut inside onto the stronger foot and finish; first-time finish from a pass or self-feed; volley from a self-feed. Collect balls between series.
coaching_points: Placement over power
Look at the goal before the ball arrives
Body over the ball to keep shots low
Follow every shot in for the rebound
progressions: Mannequin as a defender to finish around

attribution.inspired_by: Repetition finishing practised by forwards at every level, with the focus on placement and finishing from different angles

drills.name: 1v1 Moves at Game Speed
drills.description: Dribble at a cone or mannequin 'defender', perform a move at about 1.5-2 m distance (step-over, scissors, body feint, Cruyff turn, La Croqueta), then accelerate away through a gate. One move per set, then free choice.
coaching_points: Attack the defender at speed
Do the move at the right distance, not too early
Explode out of the move: the acceleration beats the defender
Use both directions
progressions: Partner as a passive then active defender
Finish on goal after the move

attribution.inspired_by: Move training in the style of Coerver Coaching; moves like the Cruyff turn and La Croqueta are named after or associated with the players who made them famous

drills.name: Reactive Agility: Colour Calls

players.note: Needs someone to call the colours

drills.description: The player stands in the middle of a square of four coloured cones. The partner calls a colour or points, and the player sprints to touch that cone and returns to the middle. Progress by doing it with a ball.
coaching_points: Low centre of gravity, quick first step
React to the call, don't guess
Short steps when changing direction
progressions: Dribble the ball to the cone
Visual signal instead of a call

attribution.inspired_by: Reactive (cue-based) agility drills, used in modern athletic development because they combine change of direction with decision-making

drills.name: Defensive Midfielder: Receive & Switch

players.note: Partner plays as centre-back; a second partner as the wide target is ideal

drills.description: The partner (as a centre-back) plays into the defensive midfielder between two cones, with a mannequin or cone behind as a marker. The 6 scans, receives on the back foot with an open body and switches play with a driven pass to a target gate or wide player on the far side. If the partner shouts 'pressure', the 6 plays back to the centre-back and offers again.
coaching_points: Scan before the pass: know where the pressure and the free side are
Open body shape so you can play forward or wide
Driven switch: low and firm, not floated
Move to a new angle after every pass
progressions: Switch must be first or second touch

attribution.inspired_by: Position-specific receiving and switching work for a defensive midfielder (the '6'), reflecting how deep midfielders are used in possession-based teams

drills.name: Driven & Lofted Long Passing

players.note: Alone: hit to a target zone and collect; with a partner: pass to each other

drills.work_rest: 4 sets x 8 passes (alternate feet), 1 min rest
drills.description: Driven and lofted passes into a 5x5 m target zone 25-40 m away, using both feet. Alternate driven passes (low and firm) with lofted passes (dropping into the zone).
coaching_points: Approach at a slight angle
Standing foot beside the ball; lean slightly back for lofted, over the ball for driven
Strike through the middle (driven) or lower half (lofted) of the ball
Follow through towards the target
progressions: Receive and play long within two touches

attribution.inspired_by: Classic long-passing technique work used by defenders and midfielders at every level

drills.name: Timed Skill Challenge Course
drills.work_rest: 4-6 timed runs, 1 min rest between runs
drills.description: A timed course: slalom dribble through cones, turn at the end, pass through a gate, collect the ball and finish into a goal or gate. Beat your best time. Add 2 seconds for every cone touched or missed gate.
coaching_points: Speed with control: penalties cost more than you gain
Small touches in the slalom, bigger touches in open space
Stay composed for the final pass and finish
progressions: Add a move before the finish

attribution.inspired_by: Timed skill challenge to add competition and game speed to individual work

drills.name: 1v1 Gate Game

players.note: Against a partner or the coach

drills.description: 1v1 against a partner or coach. Score by dribbling through either of two gates on the opponent's end line (or into a mini goal). Swap attacker and defender each round.
coaching_points: Attacker: change speed and direction to beat the defender
Defender: show one way, stay patient
React immediately when the ball changes hands
progressions: Only one gate counts, called late by the coach

attribution.inspired_by: 1v1 duel games, a basic competitive format in youth and individual coaching
